description: Renovate's REPO-side configuration. The self-hosted half (platform,
endpoint, credentials, schedule) lives in nixos/modules/renovate.nix,
which runs `renovate` from a weekly systemd timer on the services VM —
no container and no docker socket anywhere in the loop.
WHAT THIS IS FOR. Every image in this repo is pinned to an explicit tag
by hand, and a tag nobody looks at is a tag that rots. Renovate reads
the compose files and the caddy Dockerfile, checks each pin against its
registry, and opens one PR per outdated dependency. That is the whole
job: it proposes, Idan disposes.
HOW IT MESHES WITH THE IMAGE-PIN LINT — the important part. Renovate
changes a compose `image:` tag. It cannot change tests/lib/images.nix,
which holds the content-addressed {digest, hash} the offline VM suites
load, because that file is Nix and no manager here reads Nix. So a
Renovate PR ALWAYS lands with images.nix one tag behind, and the
`image-pins` lint fails it: 'compose references with no pin in
tests/lib/images.nix'. That is by design, not an oversight. The gap is
closed by .forgejo/workflows/renovate-pins.yml, which runs
./tests/update-images.sh on the renovate/** branch and commits the
regenerated images.nix back to it. The lint is the net underneath the
whole arrangement: if the workflow never ran, or ran and failed, the PR
stays red and cannot be merged by accident.
That also means a tag Renovate invents but the registry does not have
is caught twice — update-images.sh exits 1 on an unresolvable reference,
and images.nix's `_unresolved` list makes image-pins fail on the next
run regardless.
THE TWO AUTOMERGE SWITCHES, both spelled out below rather than left to
defaults. `automerge` already defaults to false, so writing it changes
nothing — it is here so a future reader sees the pair together.
`platformAutomerge` defaults to TRUE, and it is the dangerous one: with
it on, Renovate does not merge the PR itself, it asks the FORGE to merge
it as soon as checks pass. Setting only `automerge: false` would read as
'never merges' and merge anyway the moment renovate-pins.yml turns the
PR green. Idan's rule is that every bump gets a human look; both keys
are required to honour it.
pinDigests stays FALSE, also deliberately. Renovate's digest pinning
would rewrite `image: foo:1.2.3` to `foo:1.2.3@sha256:…` in the compose
files, which is a second, competing source of digest truth — this repo
already has one, tests/lib/images.nix, generated by
tests/update-images.sh and enforced by the image-pins lint. Two digest
authorities that can disagree is strictly worse than one, and the
compose files stay readable this way.
WHAT RENOVATE IS NOT ALLOWED NEAR. enabledManagers below is an
allow-list of three, which is what keeps this bot away from everything
else: no `nix` manager, so nixos/flake.lock and headscale-vps/flake.lock
are untouched (`nfu` stays a deliberate manual act, and the
flake-input-parity lint pins the two locks to each other anyway); no
`github-actions` manager, so .github/workflows and .forgejo/workflows
are untouched. Nothing here reads .nix or .sops.* files at all, so
ssh-pubkeys.nix and every secret file are outside its reach by
construction rather than by rule. If that ever stopped being true, the
sops-declared, ssh-pubkey-parity and flake-input-parity lints all run on
every branch and would fail the PR.
ignorePaths RESTATES Renovate's two defaults (node_modules,
bower_components) before adding .claude/**, because setting the key
replaces the default list rather than extending it. .claude/** holds
Claude Code worktrees — full stale copies of this repo, whose compose
files would otherwise be scanned as if they were live stacks. It is
belt-and-braces: the directory is gitignored (`*.claude` in .gitignore)
so it is not in the clone Renovate makes, and tests/update-images.sh
carries the same exclusion for the same reason.
Caddy is FOUR coupled pins across two files and must move as one PR.
stacks/caddy/Dockerfile builds a fork image with the cloudflare-dns
plugin: two `FROM caddy:` lines, the version xcaddy COMPILES, and the
plugin tag; stacks/caddy/compose.yaml then pins the published fork
tag, which mirrors the caddy version. The Dockerfile's own header
spells out why a partial bump is worse than none: the tag would say
one thing and the binary in root's TLS terminator would be another.
Grouping by path is what keeps them atomic — a reviewer sees one
diff with all four moves in it, or none.
packageRules.groupName: caddy (fork image: both FROMs, the xcaddy version, the plugin, the published tag)

description: ghcr.io/idanreed/caddy-cloudflare does not exist as an upstream
package to look up — it is OUR build output, produced by
.github/workflows/build-caddy.yml, and its tag is by convention the
upstream caddy version it wraps. So the docker-compose manager's
view of it is disabled here and the caddy-fork-tag custom manager
below re-adds the same line with depName `caddy`, i.e. resolved
against the upstream registry. Net effect: the fork tag moves in
lockstep with the Dockerfile, inside the caddy group above.
(tests/update-images.sh has the mirror of this fact in its
SUBSTITUTES table, which is what lets the offline suites pull
upstream caddy in place of an image that is not published yet.)
NO MAJOR BUMPS FOR THE RELATIONAL DATASTORES. A postgres or
mariadb major is not a tag change, it is a migration: the on-disk
data directory is version-specific, so the container comes up,
refuses the datadir, and the stack is down until someone does a dump
and restore. Several stacks here pin a major deliberately (the
17.9-alpine pins are a decision, not an oversight). Minor and patch
updates still flow — those are the security fixes and they are safe.
A real major upgrade is a planned piece of work with the restore
drill (tests/run.sh restore) in front of it, not a PR to rubber-stamp.
The caddy version xcaddy COMPILES. The dockerfile manager sees only
the two `FROM caddy:` lines; this RUN argument decides what binary
is actually built and copied over them, and leaving it behind is the
exact desync the Dockerfile header warns about. The leading `v` sits
OUTSIDE the capture group on purpose — Renovate rewrites only the
captured span, so `v2.11.2` becomes `v2.12.0` while the docker
datasource is queried with the bare `2.11.2` that its tags use.
The caddy-dns/cloudflare plugin. Unpinned this used to resolve to
whatever was latest at build time, which put unreviewed upstream
code into the process that terminates TLS for ~40 vhosts and holds a
Cloudflare API token. It is pinned, and a bump is a four-file diff
the Dockerfile header tells you to read — which is exactly what a PR
is for.
The published fork tag, resolved against UPSTREAM caddy — see the
packageRule above that disables the docker-compose manager for this
same line. Without this, bumping the Dockerfile would leave
compose.yaml pinning the old fork tag and the two would drift.
